RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

The all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — it's a procedural weakness. Many all-male panels pick well-qualified women. As a standalone argument it's easy to dismiss and makes you look like you're reaching.

It's worth more as context alongside your stronger points: fifteen years versus eight, five of them as deputy, and a stated criterion ("strong digital media experience") that may have been weighted after the fact. The unanswered request for written reasons is your best lever — most public broadcasters have an obligation to provide one.

So: chase the written explanation first. Mention panel composition as a question about process, not an accusation. If the reasons come back thin, revisit it.
